image_description: A close-up, macro shot of a vintage audio cassette tape. The casing is a translucent, yellowed plastic (indicating age). Two circular spool hubs are clearly visible in the center. There is extensive handwritten text in black ink on the label areas above and below the spools. A rectangular window for the tape head is visible between the spools. The bottom edge shows structural details like screw holes and ridges.

artifact_observations.location: Handwritten text on upper and lower label areas
artifact_observations.reasoning: The handwritten text mimics the visual flow of writing but lacks legible character structure. Letters merge into each other, and some strokes float or terminate unnaturally. It is recognizable as 'writing' but fails to form coherent words upon close inspection.

artifact_observations.location: Plastic surface near the top edge and around the text
artifact_observations.reasoning: The texture of the plastic is slightly uneven and 'muddy' in areas where the text overlaps the casing. There is a slight lack of sharp specular highlights that would be expected on smooth plastic, giving it a slightly soft, painted look rather than a molded one.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a cassette and not a similar rectangular electronic component.

focus_areas: Legibility and stroke consistency of the handwritten text
Physical depth and connectivity of the spool holes (are they true holes?)
Material realism of the aged/yellowed plastic
Geometric symmetry of the spool placement

Verify if the text auditor confirms this is non-functional gibberish.
